description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related metrics vary with initial confidence on the MMLU Pro benchmark. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0.81 to 0.99 with tick labels shown at irregular steps (including 0.81, 0.82, 0.84, 0.85, then every 0.01 from 0.86 through 0.99). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and spans 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced ticks at 0.2 intervals. Three lines with error bars are shown: the “Final Accuracy” series is a blue solid line with circular markers that starts near 1.00 at 0.81, stays in the high range around ~0.87–0.98 across the axis (e.g., ~0.90 at 0.86, ~0.97 at 0.90, ~0.86 at 0.95), and ends near ~0.98 at 0.99; the “Δ Accuracy” series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers that begins around ~0.46 at 0.81, declines to ~0.31 at 0.84 and ~0.14 at 0.86, rises and falls through mid-range values (e.g., ~0.37 at 0.88, ~0.15 at 0.89, ~0.30 at 0.93), and then decreases toward the end to ~0.11 at 0.98 and ~0.04 at 0.99; the “Initial Accuracy” series is a green dash-dot line with square markers that starts around ~0.54 at 0.81, varies upward and downward through the middle (e.g., ~0.63 at 0.84, ~0.76 at 0.86, ~0.58 at 0.88, ~0.75 at 0.89, ~0.65 at 0.91), and increases toward the right side to ~0.82 at 0.98 and ~0.93 at 0.99.
caption_used: This line plot examines the relationship between initial confidence and various accuracy metrics on the MMLU Pro benchmark. The x-axis, labeled 'Initial Confidence,' spans from 0.81 to 0.99, while the y-axis, labeled 'Accuracy,' ranges from 0.0 to 1.0. Three series are depicted: a blue solid line with square markers representing 'Final Accuracy,' which remains consistently high, starting at approximately 0.95 and stabilizing around 0.98 across the confidence spectrum. An orange dashed line with diamond markers illustrates 'Δ Accuracy,' which begins at roughly 0.45, exhibits a sharp decline to approximately 0.10 by an initial confidence of 0.86, and then fluctuates modestly before collapsing to near zero at higher confidence levels. The green dashed line with circular markers denotes 'Initial Accuracy,' which initiates at about 0.55, demonstrates a gradual upward trend, and consistently exceeds the Δ Accuracy series by a margin of at least 0.30 throughout the confidence range. Error bars indicate variability, with the Δ Accuracy series displaying the most pronounced fluctuations. The data suggest that while final accuracy remains robust, initial accuracy and the change in accuracy exhibit divergent trajectories as confidence increases.
